info.title: pond, the stick's status daemon
info.description: The HTTP API of pond (pond/README.rst), which the panel uses. Every route but /api/health and /api/auth/login needs a session (the cookie pond_sid) or the token of scripts (Authorization: Bearer). A change made in a session carries the header X-Pond. A change that gives root, or that a person checks a connection by, carries root's password in X-Pond-Password as well; five wrong passwords hold every such change, and sign-ins from that address, back for half a minute. Values are read with /api/get/ID and changed with POST /api/set/ID, whose body is KEY=VALUE lines. Over HTTP, every route but /api/health is sent on to HTTPS.

LanInfo.description: A network of the stick's towards the devices behind it, out through one connection that makes the stick their router; a connection may have several, each IPv6 one in a /64 of its own of the connection's prefix.

ipv6.description: IPv6 for its devices, by SLAAC: the /64 network @ipv6_subnet (hex) of the prefix its connection has from the operator. None from a stick of before.

LeaseInfo.description: A device behind the stick that has an address from its DHCP server: the value leases is a list of them, of every network.

name.description: The name it gave itself, if any.

ipv6.description: The global IPv6 addresses the stick sees it use (its neighbours), the ones it made by SLAAC.

ForwardInfo.description: A port forwarded from the internet, by the NAT of a router connection, to a device of one of its local networks (@lan): by its MAC, whose fixed address it goes to.

name.description: A name for it given by hand; empty for none.

conn.description: The connection it comes in by: "pppoe:N" or "ipoe:N".

ext_from.description: The ports it comes in on, first and last (the same for one).

lan.description: The device: its network and MAC, and the first of the ports it goes to.

RuleInfo.description: A firewall rule: what it lets through or blocks, from where to where. The first rule that traffic matches decides; what none matches, the defaults (FwDefaults) do.

name.description: A name for it given by hand; empty for none.

from.description: Where it comes from and goes to: "internet", or a part of it as "internet:ADDR/LEN"; "lans", every local network; "lan:N", one; or "dev:N:MAC", a device of network N by its MAC.

ports.description: The ports it goes to, of TCP or UDP: "" for every one, "443", "8000-8100".

FwDefaults.description: What the firewall does where no rule decides: from the local networks to the internet, and between them. From the internet in it always blocks, but for the forwards and the DMZ (NAT). And whether the stick answers a ping from the internet and from the LANs, block where the stick says nothing; on the management VLAN it always does.

DmzInfo.description: A connection's DMZ: the device that takes what comes in that no forward takes.

FixedInfo.description: A device's fixed address: in its network, its MAC always gets the same IP.

name.description: A name for it given by hand, which the panel shows before its own; empty for none.

address.description: The management pair's new address, with its prefix.

ipoe.description: The connections that take their address as a router does; absent on a stick of before.

lans.description: The networks behind the stick, and their devices' fixed addresses; absent on a stick of before. The devices with an address are a value of their own, leases (LeaseInfo), which the settings do not carry.

rules.description: The firewall's rules, in their order.

mode.description: passthrough with sessions, bridge without, as onu-apply brought it up.

pass.description: peer_gateway: the concentrator's address, when the router has it as its gateway.

trials.description: The changes on trial: each goes back at until_s, in seconds of the stick's uptime, unless the panel confirms it; the management pair's only from a panel opened at its new address. Absent on a stick of before.

Tls.description: The panel's HTTPS: the certificate of each address it answers on (pond's "tls").

own.description: An own certificate, which an authority signed and the stick serves on every address in place of those it signs itself; null without one.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the certificate, as browsers show it: "AB:CD:...".

named.description: Whether the certificate names the address; the stick's own always do.

subject.description: The common name and the organisation, as words: "O=Example, CN=stick.example".

chain.description: The certificates the stick sends, its own first.

Ssh.description: pond's value "ssh": the ssh server's host key and the keys root logs in with.

keys_max.description: The most keys of the panel's; the image's do not count.

type.description: "unknown" for a line of the image's file that is no key the panel reads.

fingerprint.description: "SHA256:" and unpadded base64, as ssh-keygen -l prints it; "-" when unknown.

source.description: "panel" for a key the panel added, which it may remove; "image" for one of the image's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, which nothing on the stick changes. Absent from a stick whose pond predates it: the panel's.

Sessions.description: pond's /api/auth/sessions: the sessions open, none with its id.

now_s.description: The stick's clock when it answered, which since_s and seen_s are of.

from.description: The address its sign-in came from.

TokenState.description: pond's /api/token: whether a token of scripts is in force; never the token.

Clock.description: The stick's clock (pond's value "clock"): the time it reads, and what its time daemon says of it. source and state are null without the daemon's state; a source it does not ask is null.

updated_s.description: When the daemon last wrote its state, by the stick's clock.

freq_ppb.description: The correction of the clock's frequency, ppb; positive speeds it up.

stamps.description: The stamps of PTP over layer 2: the switch's, or the kernel's.

phc_freq_ppb.description: With hardware stamps: the correction of the switch clock's (PHC) frequency, ppb.

sys_phc_offset_ns.description: With hardware stamps: the system clock less the PHC's time.

root.description: The kernel command line's root=; null when it names none, as on a RAM boot.

FirmwareBank.description: A bank of the flash as onu-update tells it.

state.description: valid, incomplete (a write cut short), empty, or shipped (the shipped firmware)

time.description: the time of its kernel image, in seconds since 1970

kernel_used_b.description: What its kernel image and root filesystem use; absent from an older stick.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bank as an update file (onu-update read), in lowercase hex: the digest of update.bin in a release's SHA256SUMS. Null while the stick reads the bank, which it does once after each start and after each write, and for a bank that holds no system of this kind.

signature.description: Its signature (onu-update): valid, made with one of the keys the stick trusts (keys); none, a file without a signature, such as one built from this repository by anyone; unknown, made with a key the stick does not trust; bad, a signature that does not match the file. Null while the stick reads the bank, and for a bank that holds no system of this kind.

signer.description: The name of the key a valid signature was made with.

Firmware.description: The two banks, the starts, and an upload under way (pond's value "firmware").

trial.description: the bank that runs on trial, not committed yet

failed.description: a bank whose trial did not come up

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file written, once it is written.

signature.description: The signature of the file written, once it is written; a bad one is not written.

keys.description: The keys whose signatures the stick trusts: those of the system that runs.

id.description: The SHA-256 of the raw public key, in lowercase hex, as a signature names its key.

public.description: The raw Ed25519 public key, 32 bytes, in base64.

Identity.description: How the stick introduces itself to the OLT. The PLOAM password is never served, only whether one is set. source says where it comes from: the stick's own store, or the shipped firmware's configuration.

loid.description: Absent from a stick whose pond predates them.

uni_report.description: The ports the stick tells the OLT of (G.988): its Ethernet UNIs, the PPTP, its VEIP, or both; and how many Ethernet UNIs, 1 to 8, as many as the ONT it stands in for has. Each is the one SFP lane. Absent from a stick whose pond predates them.

pots_ports.description: How many phone sockets (POTS UNIs) the stick tells the OLT of: 0, 1 or 2.

olt_login.description: The PPPoE login the OLT sent (Authentication security method, G.988 9.12.4), never its password, only whether there is one; null when the OLT sent none.

UniReport.description: Which ports the stick tells the OLT of: the Ethernet UNIs (PPTP), the VEIP, or both.

UniPorts.description: How many Ethernet UNIs the stick tells the OLT of.

PotsPorts.description: How many phone sockets the stick tells the OLT of.

Phone.description: pond's value "phone": the phone service the OLT set up on the stick's phone sockets, which have no wire: the SIP accounts and server through OMCI (G.988 9.9), for a VoIP device of the person's own to use. Never a password, only whether there is one.

method.description: How the OLT sets the phone up: through OMCI, through TR-069, or not at all.

lines.description: The sockets the stick tells the OLT of, each with its SIP account.

codecs.description: The codecs, in the order the OLT prefers them.

vlan.description: The VLAN of the voice: on the fibre, and to the host.

number.description: The phone number, the user part of the address of record.

ServiceRule.description: What the stick does with a service the OLT set up, on its one SFP lane: moves it to another VLAN towards the host, keeps it off the host, or keeps it to the Ethernet UNI or to the VEIP alone. The stick makes such a rule by itself when two services would reach the host in one VLAN (auto), and a person's own rule takes its place. A rule is kept by the service's VLAN on the fibre, across the OLT's setting the services up again.

fibre.description: The service, by its VLAN on the fibre; null for the one that filters none.

host.description: The VLAN towards the host, of a move alone.

auto.description: Made by the stick, for a clash; a person's own when false.

ServiceRules.description: pond's value "service_rules": the rules in force, the stick's and the person's.

Iptv.description: pond's value "iptv": television on the stick, as omcid's multicast agent holds it (omcid/README.rst, the multicast proxy): the OLT's policy, the groups the bridge forwards now, the joins it refused and the streams that stopped, the counts, the OLT's queries and the latest events. Times are the stick's clock in seconds, now_s among them.

mode.description: Snooping alone, snooping with proxy reporting, or a proxy (G.988 9.3.27, IGMP function).

max_groups.description: The most groups at once; null for no limit.

query_response_ms.description: The most time to answer a query, and to answer one about a group after a leave.

host_vlan.description: The VLAN the groups reach the host in; null when the OLT keeps the stream's tag.

allowed.description: The groups the OLT allows, as ranges, in full or for preview.

policy.description: What the OLT set in the multicast operations profile; null before it set one.

client.description: The host address that joined it.

rate_bps.description: The stream's bits a second, from the bytes the switch counted; null before two counts.

groups.description: The groups the bridge forwards now.

rejected.description: The joins the policy refused, the latest first.

lost.description: The groups whose stream stopped while they were joined.

querier.description: The OLT's latest query, and its IGMP version; null before one came.

pcp.description: The priority given; null when the host's goes.

auto.description: The stick gives the rules' priority where the OLT leaves it to the host.

dropped.description: The joins no rule took for their priority, while the host's went.

priority.description: The priority the subscriber's IGMP goes up with. The profile's upstream IGMP tag control (G.988 9.3.27): 0 the VLAN rules, 1 a tag added, 2 the tag replaced, 3 its VID replaced. At 1 and 2 the OLT's tag gives it; at 0 and 3 the host's would, and the stick gives the one the operator's rules take in the VLAN instead, unless a person turned that off.

log.description: The latest events, the newest first.

IptvTest.description: What a test of a group measured: the stick joins it, counts its stream's bytes, and leaves.

first_ms.description: The milliseconds until the first frame; null when none came.

PhoneSecrets.description: The SIP passwords of the phone's lines, which root's password shows.

OltLogin.description: The PPPoE login the OLT sent, with its password (secret), which root's password shows.

realm.description: The realm the OLT sent beside them, empty for none.

LaneMode.description: The modes of the SFP lane, the driver's: its own search, or one of four it keeps to.

SfpLane.description: The SFP lane (pond's value "sfp_lane"): the mode chosen, the one the lane runs in now (null while it looks for the host), and a change on trial, which the stick undoes at until_s (seconds of uptime) unless it is kept.

Mgmt.description: The management VLAN and address (pond's value "mgmt"), and a new pair added beside them that waits to be confirmed from a panel opened at it.

data_address.description: An address on the SFP port itself, without a VLAN; empty in production.

OmciValue.description: What the OLT set up, as omcid holds it: each instance of the classes pond reads, every attribute in hexadecimal (null for a password), and which of them are tables, whose value is the rows end to end.

OmciFrame.description: A frame of the conversation with the OLT, as omcid keeps it: its number from omcid's start, the wall clock when it passed, what omcid did with it (its enum omci_ctl_tap_verdict), its message type, whether the logical password was zeroed in it, and the frame in hexadecimal.

OmciFrames.description: The frames from a number on: the next one's number, and the oldest kept.

Link.description: One network interface: a switch port, a VLAN, a GEM port, a bridge, a PPP link.

kind.description: "dsa" for a switch port, "vlan", "gem", "bridge", "ppp"; null for the CPU port.

lower.description: The device it runs over: a VLAN's port, a switch port's conduit.

destination.description: "default", or an address with its prefix length.

parent.description: The qdisc the rule is on (tcm_parent).

match.description: What the rule matches; null for a key it does not match on.

match_unparsed.description: The numbers of the flower attributes the rule has and pond does not read.

options_decoded.description: false for a rule whose options pond does not read, which then has no match, actions or offload.

TcRules.description: The rules on each port's way in: a list, or why it could not be read.
